reasons: The claimed gap is supported by the cited text: Section 10.1 only ends access after an undefined 'agreed transition period' and 10.2 addresses Deliverables and refunds, so no Vendor obligation to assist with migration, return/export Customer Data, or delete and certify deletion exists in the termination section.

The inserted Section 10.3 tracks the playbook preferred position element-by-element (up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return/export, subsequent deletion with written certification) and is placed correctly in the termination section as new 10.3 following p0042.

Edit is directionally pro-customer and minimal — it adds a new clause without altering surrounding operative language; extending the trigger to 'or any Order Form' and permitting routine-backup/legal-retention carve-outs are customary, do not reach the walk-away line (no data return or immediate deletion), and keep the ask negotiable.
Comment complies with tone and content requirements: first person plural, states what was added and why, cites the playbook position and offers the 90-day fallback without lecturing.
Deterministic checks confirm the operation applies and that data-return/transition language is present in the resulting text.
